title: Admit configuration once, before it can change the corpus
problem: The runtime, doctor and editor schema own different fragments of the configuration contract; malformed string collections can silently remove the scored corpus.
proposed_change: Give the configuration module one complete admission contract for collection, string, numeric and boolean fields; derive the editor and diagnostic field facts from that contract.
evidence: Disposable CLI replay: paths="src" yields inventory exit 0 with zero files and zero functions.
Five in-memory inputs rejected by the published schema are accepted by load_config_text; exclude.globs="tests/**" becomes eight one-character patterns, including '*'.
Sixteen existing schema, CLI-documentation and subprocess-coverage contract tests still pass.
after: Valid corpus inputs + derived field facts
deletion_test: Delete repeated field declarations and coercions; preserve one admission implementation instead of moving validation into every command.
locality: A field changes in one module.
test_benefits: Check invalid shapes through load_config_text and inventory; compare generated schema semantics.
cost_risk: Medium. Preserve current supported TOML and nearest-root behavior; avoid adding a runtime schema framework.

title: Make hosted CI judge the full CRAP verdict
problem: The hosted matrix enforces changed-function CCN, while the self-Action disables gate and delta; it never proves a baseline-aware CRAP verdict on the pull request.
proposed_change: Build and install the base and candidate wheels in separate hosted test environments, bind each artifact to its source, then run the actual CRAP verdict against the event base.
evidence: ci.yml invokes hook-precommit --base on Ubuntu/Python 3.12, then configures the dogfood Action with gate=false and delta=false.
The workflow records why an editable candidate installation makes a base worktree import the candidate source; the missing isolation is known in current source.
The current wheel builds and imports successfully in a disposable archive, but CI only tests editable installations.
after: Coverage artifacts bound to each tree
deletion_test: Replace the non-gating self-run with verified artifact ownership; retain the platform matrix and reuse its evidence only when inputs are proven.
leverage: One proof covers installation and verdict.
test_benefits: A disposable coverage-only regression must fail hosted verification while unchanged code passes.
cost_risk: Medium. Base setup adds runner time; preserve subprocess measurement and never reuse artifacts across installations without proof.

title: Build once and resume release publication by surface
problem: stage2b pushes the tag before building artifacts and restarts the whole publication stage without completion checks, even after an earlier surface succeeded.
proposed_change: Have the release module build and check immutable artifacts before publishing, record their digests, and resume incomplete surfaces after reading back completed ones.
evidence: The current plan orders push, remove-dist/build/check/upload, GitHub release, plugin update, Pages build.
An in-memory success adapter records two stage2b calls requesting all five steps in the same order; real execution stops at its first failure. No external command was executed.
The receipt records contract and verify proof but no artifact digests or completed publication surfaces; current remote readback checks version presence, not artifact identity.
deletion_test: Replace operator reconstruction of partial releases with one owned release state; keep the existing surface table and live readback adapters.
locality: Artifact identity stays with release state.
test_benefits: Inject a failure after each surface and prove retry neither rebuilds nor republishes confirmed bytes.
cost_risk: Medium. Add digest-based remote artifact readback to existing version-presence checks. Real external outcomes can be uncertain; confirm artifact identity before marking a surface complete.

title: Keep operational guidance attached to its behavior
problem: Operational guidance drifts independently across pages: current references still describe live-tree mutation, support only 0.4.x and recommend parallel unit tests against the contributor contract.
proposed_change: Generate version-support and test-command snippets from their owners, retain authored behavior explanations, and link those explanations to behavioral contracts. RT1 owns configuration-field and schema generation.
evidence: docs/configuration.md:48, SECURITY.md:48 and the schema describe single-worker live-tree mutation after the implementation moved it to a disposable snapshot.
SECURITY.md lists 0.4.x as supported while pyproject.toml and the package declare 0.6.0.
CONTRIBUTING.md:29 recommends tests/unit -n 8; pyproject.toml:86 and AGENTS.md require serial in-process tests.
deletion_test: Delete duplicate command/version maintenance and corresponding phrase checks. Keep authored behavior prose and verify its claims; do not generate all prose or add another runtime registry.
test_benefits: Check generated fragments are current and documented examples exercise the supported behavior.
cost_risk: Small to medium. Agree which facts are generated; preserve stable anchors and human explanations.

title: Use the same suite schedule for development and self-verification
problem: The repo asks for serial in-process tests and eight parallel CLI workers, but its own coverage/verify lane runs every test serially.
proposed_change: Let one test-run module run in-process tests serially and isolated CLI tests in parallel, then combine coverage and JUnit evidence into the single lane's artifacts.
evidence: crapkit.toml:4 names both schedules; the lane at line 40 invokes bare pytest with no -n or suite split.
CI separately runs tests/unit and tests/e2e -n 8; pyproject deliberately defaults to serial.
This review did not benchmark a combined coverage implementation; no speedup figure is claimed.
deletion_test: Delete duplicated execution schedules; retain the distinction between state-sharing tests and isolated CLI tests.
leverage: One schedule serves CI and verify.
test_benefits: Assert both suites contribute counts and branches, and either failing suite makes the lane fail.
cost_risk: Medium. JUnit IDs, coverage contexts and subprocess measurements must survive aggregation; benchmark before adopting.
